buckets.crowd: the crowd's pathing: Crowd._physics_process() and every CrowdAgent._process()
buckets.draw: CPU side of drawing: deferred calls and _draw() callbacks after the last _process() (but the scenery queue's), then the renderer's sync and submit; no GPU time; on a native window with VSync, the buffer swap's wait
buckets.events: event updates: EventManager._physics_process() and every EventInstance._process()
buckets.physics_rest: physics steps' work no named system claims: her movement, the physics server's step, _draw() callbacks queued during physics
buckets.process_rest: process work no named system claims: main, HUD, day clock, resistance, scenery animation, the debug readout
buckets.scenery: SceneryResidency.update(): the scenery queue under its 2ms budget, guard preparations included, and the tile map work and first draws its jobs left to the deferred flush (also counted as scenery_deferred_usec); the renderer's own work on the new pictures is draw's
buckets.wait: after the post-draw callback until the next frame: idle until the refresh, plus input and window events; not a cost

clock: every microsecond value is quantized to environment.timer_resolution_usec, which on a page is the browser's reduced-precision clock

environment.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 10; K) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/154.0.0.0 Mobile Safari/537.36

gpu_time: not measured: a phone's browser offers no GPU timing, so draw_usec is the CPU side of drawing only
